title: Champagne Dance
label: So Urban / Sony

type.basis: The crew's party-friendly garage single, recorded with Wiley and Geeneus. Held as an outgroup: the same crew, in its garage mode, in the same year as Eskimo.

sound.text: Trench (2019): a memorable sung hook over bouncy, summery production, the crew's party-friendly garage mode as opposed to their darker material.
RBMA (2015): recorded at Island's Fallout Shelter studio with Geeneus and Wiley, with Matthew Herbert on keys.

context.text: Official Singles Chart peak no. 13 (first chart date 27 Apr 2002, 5 weeks); Dance chart peak no. 5.
Per RBMA (2015), Island's MD rejected it and Sony signed it.
Wikipedia calls it the crew's only charting hit before they split; members went on to the grime crew Roll Deep.

calls.label: mainstream garage hit / UK garage crossover

rels.other: Pay As U Go – Know We (2000)

uncertainty: Year conflicts: Trench and FACT place it in 2001; OCC and Wikipedia give 2002. Peak conflicts: RBMA says no. 12, but OCC shows no. 13. Label naming differs (OCC: So Urban; Wikipedia: Sony Music; So Urban was presumably a Sony imprint, which is not verified). Producer not credited in the sources. It is included as the garage-facing counterpart to 'Know We'; no source calls it grime.
tracklist: 12-inch: A 'Brown Acid Mix'; B1 'Da Sticky Lick'; B2 'Destruction Remix'. CD: Brown Acid Radio Edit / Da Sticky Lick / Destruction Remix / video. Writers include Richard Cowie Jr (Wiley) and Darren Joseph (DJ Target).
